_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Saharan Rock Art and Early Peoples
910.label: Event
910.description: The Ennedi and Tibesti massifs preserve stunning Saharan rock art depicting a green Sahara; pastoralist and agricultural communities thrive before desertification.

910.name: Ennedi and Tibesti Rock Art
910.label: Event
910.description: Rock paintings and engravings in the Ennedi Plateau and Tibesti Mountains show cattle herding, hunting, and ritual scenes from the African Humid Period.

910.name: Green Sahara Desiccation and Migration
910.label: Event
910.description: Sahara dries out; populations migrate southward to the Lake Chad basin and Sahel; foundation for later sedentary civilisations.

910.name: Sao Civilisation
910.label: Event
910.description: The Sao people build walled settlements around Lake Chad; terracotta and bronze artistic traditions; eventually absorbed by Kanem-Bornu.

910.name: Sao Walled Settlements and Art
910.label: Event
910.description: Sao communities construct mound settlements in the Lake Chad floodplain; renowned terracotta figurines and funerary traditions.

910.name: Sao Absorption into Kanem-Bornu
910.label: Event
910.description: Kanem Empire gradually incorporates Sao communities; Kotoko city-states emerge as Sao successor polities.

920.name: Kanem Empire
920.label: Event
920.description: The Kanem Empire, ruled by the Saifawa dynasty, dominates the Lake Chad region; Islam adopted c.1085; trans-Saharan trade flourishes.

920.name: Rise of the Saifawa Dynasty
920.label: Event
920.description: Duguwa and Saifawa rulers unite Kanem; control of trans-Saharan trade routes linking Fezzan and the Nile Valley.

920.name: Islamisation of Kanem
920.label: Event
920.description: Mai Hummay adopts Islam c.1085; Kanem becomes a centre of Islamic learning; diplomatic links with North Africa and Egypt.

920.name: Bornu Empire
920.label: Event
920.description: The Saifawa dynasty re-establishes power west of Lake Chad as the Bornu Empire; Idris Alooma's golden age; gradual decline.

920.name: Bornu Renaissance under Idris Alooma
920.label: Event
920.description: Mai Idris Alooma modernises the army with firearms; diplomatic ties with Ottoman Tripoli; Bornu recaptures Kanem heartland.

920.name: Bornu Decline and Rabih az-Zubayr
920.label: Event
920.description: Fulani jihad pressures Bornu; El-Kanemi sheikhs supplant Saifawa; Rabih az-Zubayr conquers Bornu 1893; end of millennium-old dynasty.

930.name: Wadai and Bagirmi Sultanates
930.label: Event
930.description: The Sultanate of Wadai and the Kingdom of Bagirmi emerge as major powers east and south of Lake Chad; slave trading and Islamic culture.

930.name: Kingdom of Bagirmi
930.label: Event
930.description: Bagirmi kingdom centered on Massenya; vassal to Bornu then Wadai; slave raiding in the south; French conquest 1897.

930.name: Sultanate of Wadai
930.label: Event
930.description: Wadai sultanate centred on Abéché; controls Saharan trade routes to Benghazi; defeats Bornu influence; last independent sultanate falls to France 1912.

940.name: French Conquest and Colonial Chad
940.label: Event
940.description: France conquers Chad in stages; Territoire Militaire du Tchad within AEF; forced cotton cultivation in the south; Félix Éboué rallies Chad to Free France.

940.name: French Conquest and Battle of Kousséri
940.label: Event
940.description: Three French columns converge and defeat Rabih at Kousséri (1900); progressive pacification of the north; last Senoussi resistance 1920.

940.name: Colonial Exploitation: Le Tchad Utile
940.label: Event
940.description: France develops only 'le Tchad utile' (useful south); forced cotton cultivation; Muslim north neglected; Éboué rallies Chad to Free France 1940; post-war political awakening.

950.name: Independence and Tombalbaye Era
950.label: Event
950.description: François (Ngarta) Tombalbaye leads independence; southern Christian domination; northern Muslim rebellion (FROLINAT); increasing authoritarianism and assassination.

950.name: Independence and One-Party Rule
950.label: Event
950.description: Chad independent 11 August 1960; Tombalbaye's PPT becomes sole party; southern-dominated government alienates the Muslim north.

950.name: FROLINAT Northern Rebellion
950.label: Event
950.description: Front de Libération Nationale du Tchad (FROLINAT) launches insurgency; French military intervention (Operation Bison); Tombalbaye assassinated in military coup April 1975.

950.name: Civil Wars and Libyan Intervention
950.label: Event
950.description: Chadian civil wars intensify; Libya annexes the Aouzou Strip; Habré and Goukouni factions clash; Toyota War drives out Libyan forces.

950.name: Malloum, Habré, and Goukouni Power Struggles
950.label: Event
950.description: General Malloum overthrown; Goukouni's GUNT vs Habré's FAN; Libyan troops invited then expelled; Habré seizes N'Djamena 1982.

950.name: Libyan-Chadian Conflict and Toyota War
950.label: Event
950.description: Gaddafi's Libya occupies Aouzou Strip and intervenes repeatedly; Toyota War (1987) sees Chad rout Libyan forces using pickup trucks; ICJ awards Aouzou to Chad 1994.

960.name: Déby Dynasty and Contemporary Chad
960.label: Event
960.description: Idriss Déby seizes power 1990; 30-year rule; oil revenues; regional military power; killed in battle 2021; son Mahamat Déby takes over.

960.name: Idriss Déby's Rise and Consolidation
960.label: Event
960.description: Déby overthrows Habré December 1990; multiparty constitution 1996; eliminates term limits; oil pipeline to Cameroon opens 2003.

960.name: Oil Revenues and Regional Power
960.label: Event
960.description: Doba oil fields transform economy; World Bank transparency experiment fails; Chad becomes key French and US counterterrorism partner in Sahel.
